item.title: Alotau hospital marks World Heart Day with focus on health worker screening
item.description: The Alotau Provincial Hospital in Milne Bay Province commemorated World Heart Day with Non-communicable Disease [NCD] screening under the global theme 'Don't Miss a Beat'.‎‎ The World Heart Day is observed globally on 29 September annually, aimed at raising awareness on detection and prevention of cardiovascular diseases.‎‎
item.content:encoded:
The Alotau Provincial Hospital in Milne Bay Province commemorated World Heart Day with Non-communicable Disease [NCD] screening under the global theme 'Don't Miss a Beat'.‎‎

The World Heart Day is observed globally on 29 September annually, aimed at raising awareness on detection and prevention of cardiovascular diseases.‎‎

The two-day program, led by APH Internal Medicine and the Public Health disease control team, commenced yesterday and concludes today at the At40 clinic. ‎‎Staff members of the Milne Bay Provincial Health Authority [MBPHA] at its heardquarters in Alotau were at the center of the screening process.

The MBPHA chief executive officer Dr Perista Mamadi was first to undergo this screening yesterday.‎‎

The screening includes blood pressure and hypertension checks, blood sugar testing, body mass index, and general assessment of cardiovascular risks factors.‎‎

The initiative is aligned with the global World Heart Day campaign which promotes early detection and prevention of heart diseases.‎‎

With the two-days program focused on screening health workers, APH physician Dr Dennis Tony says the wellbeing of every health worker is paramount.

‎‎"Strengthening early detection and management of cardiovascular risks factors across our health workers is very important," he said.

"We believe this program will bring a meaningful contribution to reducing the burden of non-communicable diseases among our health workers.

‎‎"We would also like to ensure that all our medical staff are well and healthy to provide care to patients and clients."‎‎

Meanwhile, Disease Control Coordinator and Acting Deputy Director of Public Health, Tony Lota said lifestyle choices can have a direct impact on heart health.

‎‎"Smoking, continuous intake of fatty foods, excessive intake of alcohol and lack of physical exercise can put a strain on the heart's health," he said.

‎‎Lota is encouraging everyone to take their health seriously and undergo regular medical check-ups to ensure that the heart is healthy.‎‎

The World Heart Day screening is part of APH and MBPHA's ongoing efforts to address risking burden of non-communicable diseases in Milne Bay Province.‎‎

item.title: PNG Power expands Port Moresby blackouts to four-hour blocks as El Niño and technical fault hit supply
item.description: PNG Power has increased load shedding across the National Capital District and Central Province to four-hour rotational blocks following a fresh 28-megawatt supply loss caused by a technical fault. The power utility confirmed on Tuesday morning that Transmission Line L545, which connects the independent power producer Dirio Power Station to the Konedobu Substation, suffered a failure.
item.content:encoded:
PNG Power has increased load shedding across the National Capital District and Central Province to four-hour rotational blocks following a fresh 28-megawatt supply loss caused by a technical fault.

The power utility confirmed on Tuesday morning that Transmission Line L545, which connects the independent power producer Dirio Power Station to the Konedobu Substation, suffered a failure.

The latest fault compounds an existing generation shortfall caused by falling water levels at the Sirinumu Dam due to the severe El Niño drought affecting the southern region.

PNG Power said technical teams are on site attempting to locate and repair the line fault.

The company confirmed that output from the Rouna and Edevu hydro power stations cannot be increased due to strict water conservation measures currently enforced at Sirinumu.

The four-hour rotational blackouts represent an escalation from the previous two-hour load-shedding schedule.

PNG Power advised that the two-hour schedule will resume once Line L545 is restored and additional generation capacity returns to the grid.

The utility has appealed to residential, commercial, and industrial consumers across Port Moresby and Central Province to conserve electricity and water.

Consumers have been urged to turn off non-essential appliances and avoid high power usage during peak demand hours, set between 9am and 4pm, and from 6pm to 8pm.

PNG Power stated that its priority remains preserving remaining water reserves at Sirinumu Dam to sustain both electricity generation and the capital's municipal water supply through the extended dry spell.

item.title: ENB scales down classes as dry spell hits schools
item.description: Schools in East New Britain province have scaled down classes due to severe water shortage and hygiene problems caused by the prolonged dry spell. Acting provincial Education Advisor Paius Reva issued a circular last Friday, advising all schools to adjust their programs during the drought period.
item.content:encoded:
Schools in East New Britain province have scaled down classes due to severe water shortage and hygiene problems caused by the prolonged dry spell.

Acting provincial Education Advisor Paius Reva issued a circular last Friday, advising all schools to adjust their programs during the drought period.

In the circular, Reva stated that all Early Childhood Learning Centres have been suspended indefinitely since Friday. He said classes from elementary to grade 7 and grades 9 and 11 have also been scaled down.

"Schools across the country, and particularly in East New Britain Province, are experiencing severe and divergent weather extremes," he said. "The drought has caused critical water shortages, poor sanitation, crop failure, food-related health issues, and low student attendance."

Reva said Grades 8, 10 and 12 will only come to school on certain days until their national exams.

He said the decision was made after most water sources at schools dried up.

"Many schools depend on rainwater tanks and local water creeks which have now dried up, and primary schools are the most severely affected in the province."

The Education Board is advising parents to keep children at home and ensure they practice good hygiene during the drought period.

item.title: Minister Namah officiates at UNRE World Tourism Day celebrations
item.description: Minister for Tourism, Arts and Culture, Belden Namah, has officiated at the Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment [PNG UNRE] Culture and Tourism Day celebrations at the Vudal Campus in East New Britain. Namah attended the event as guest of honour as part of a two-day official visit to the province.
item.content:encoded:
Minister for Tourism, Arts and Culture, Belden Namah, has officiated at the Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment [PNG UNRE] Culture and Tourism Day celebrations at the Vudal Campus in East New Britain.

Namah attended the event as guest of honour as part of a two-day official visit to the province.

His visit included a groundbreaking ceremony for the John Momis Ocean and Climate Research Institute at Vunavutung and the launching of the university's commercial arm, NR & E Corporation Limited, in Rabaul.

Speaking at the Vudal Campus, Namah praised the university council and administration for combining higher education, research, and cultural preservation into practical tourism initiatives.

"I commend the wisdom of the university council for demonstrating how education, research, culture, and tourism can work together," Namah said.

PNG UNRE has offered a Bachelor of Sustainable International Tourism under its School of Sustainable Resource Management and Business Studies since 2018, establishing itself as a premier institution for tourism studies in the country.

Namah announced that the national government plans to formalize strategic partnerships with the university before the end of the year to drive economic growth through sustainable tourism.

"Before this year ends, I will ensure UNRE signs a memorandum of understanding with the PNG Tourism Promotion Authority, the National Cultural Commission, and the National Museum and Art Gallery," he said.

"UNRE will become the centre of excellence in preserving our natural resources, our culture, and our traditions."

Following its inauguration, the PNG UNRE Culture and World Tourism Day has been officially listed on the National Cultural Commission's annual events calendar, aligned with global World Tourism Day commemorations on September 27.

Namah reassured the university that the ministry will continue providing structural and financial support for tertiary tourism programs and cultural preservation.

item.title: Schools move to half-day classes as El Niño drought hits Bougainville
item.description: Schools across North Bougainville have been forced to implement half-day instruction following severe water shortages caused by ongoing El Niño drought conditions. Autonomous Bougainville Government [ABG] Education Secretary Dorothy Kenneth said the temporary timetable took effect on Monday and will remain in place until further notice.
item.content:encoded:
Schools across North Bougainville have been forced to implement half-day instruction following severe water shortages caused by ongoing El Niño drought conditions.

Autonomous Bougainville Government [ABG] Education Secretary Dorothy Kenneth said the temporary timetable took effect on Monday and will remain in place until further notice.

Under the emergency schedule, classes operate from 9am until midday, allowing students to return home before peak afternoon heat. Teachers are using the afternoons to secure household water supplies for their families and prepare home-learning materials for students.

Ms Kenneth said North Bougainville has experienced worsening water scarcity since Term Three, creating significant hygiene and welfare risks for both students and teaching staff.

While North Bougainville faces severe dry conditions, South Bougainville is currently experiencing heavy rainfall and flooding. Central Bougainville has so far reported no major climate disruptions.

The Education Department warned that schools in other regions may also adopt shortened hours if conditions deteriorate.

Ms Kenneth emphasized that the primary focus remains protecting the health and safety of students and staff while maintaining educational continuity through the dry spell.

item.title: Hela firearm amnesty moves to Hayapuga LLG following mass surrenders
item.description: Preparations are under way in Hela Province for another major illegal firearm surrender program scheduled to take place on Wednesday in the Hayapuga Local Level Government [LLG] area. The event at Hiwanda Primary School in the Tari-Pori District follows significant weapon surrenders across the province in recent days.
item.content:encoded:
Preparations are under way in Hela Province for another major illegal firearm surrender program scheduled to take place on Wednesday in the Hayapuga Local Level Government [LLG] area.

The event at Hiwanda Primary School in the Tari-Pori District follows significant weapon surrenders across the province in recent days.

On Thursday, community members in Tebi LLG handed in 18 factory-made firearms. In neighboring Tagali LLG, 47 factory-manufactured guns were turned over to authorities.

The tallies do not include dozens of homemade firearms, hand grenades, bows, arrows, and wire catapults surrendered alongside the military-grade weapons.

Hela Governor Philip Undialu thanked community leaders, youth groups, and churches for driving the peace initiative ahead of the deadline for the government's official gun amnesty.

"We have two months remaining before the official amnesty period comes to an end," Undialu said.

"I am deeply encouraged by the overwhelming cooperation shown by our communities, guided by local church groups, LLG presidents, and ward councilors. We have all experienced the devastating toll and pain that gun violence and tribal conflicts bring to our province."

Following the Hayapuga program, the amnesty drive will move to Tari Urban and Pori LLGs.

Authorities plan to expand the program across the Koroba-Lake Kopiago, Komo-Hulia, and Magarima districts over the coming weeks.

item.title: Marape praises Trump, Xi meeting as PNG maintains diplomatic balance
item.description: Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape has praised a high-level meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, saying stable relations between the two global powers are crucial for world trade and regional stability. Marape said Papua New Guinea would continue to maintain close, balanced ties with both superpowers.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea Prime Minister James Marape has praised a high-level meeting between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington, saying stable relations between the two global powers are crucial for world trade and regional stability.

Marape said Papua New Guinea would continue to maintain close, balanced ties with both superpowers.

"Papua New Guinea maintains close relations with both the United States and China, and we welcome continued dialogue and cooperation between Washington and Beijing," Marape said.

The Prime Minister said PNG's relationship with the US had gained momentum following his recent attendance at the 81st United Nations General Assembly [UNGA] in New York, where he met President Trump.

"President Trump provided assurances of support for strengthening PNG-US relations, particularly through greater involvement by American private-sector companies," Marape said.

He said discussions with a US business delegation in New York outlined growing commercial interest in PNG's agriculture, fisheries, manufacturing, technology, mining, and energy sectors.

At the same time, Marape reaffirmed Port Moresby's commitment to its long-standing 'One China' policy.

He said he expects to meet President Xi on the sidelines of the upcoming Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation [APEC] summit to discuss expanding trade and investment ties.

item.title: PNG advocates localized prevention at UN peacebuilding meeting
item.description: Papua New Guinea’s Minister for Foreign Affairs Justin Tkatchenko has called on the international community to prioritize national ownership and community-led prevention in global peacebuilding efforts. Addressing the 2026 Peacebuilding Commission Ministerial-Level Meeting in New York on September 24, Tkatchenko emphasized that international assistance must align with nationally determined priorit
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea’s Minister for Foreign Affairs Justin Tkatchenko has called on the international community to prioritize national ownership and community-led prevention in global peacebuilding efforts.

Addressing the 2026 Peacebuilding Commission Ministerial-Level Meeting in New York on September 24, Tkatchenko emphasized that international assistance must align with nationally determined priorities rather than replace them.

“External assistance cannot be a substitute for national ownership,” Tkatchenko told delegates. “The international community is most effective when it supports nationally determined priorities, strengthens national institutions, and helps societies develop their own capacity to prevent and resolve conflict.”

Speaking about Papua New Guinea’s experiences, Tkatchenko cited the Bougainville peace process, which marks 25 years of peace following the 2001 Bougainville Peace Agreement and the subsequent 2025 Melanesian Agreement, as a benchmark for resolving complex disputes through peaceful dialogue and constitutional channels.

He also spoke about PNG’s National Prevention Strategy [2025–2030], launched in late 2025 in partnership with the United Nations. The whole-of-society initiative engages business groups, churches, women's organizations and youth groups to address the root causes of conflict and social violence.

Tkatchenko said emerging conflicts are increasingly exacerbated by poverty, weak institutions and climate change, describing climate impacts as an existential security threat to small island developing states.

He urged global leaders to move away from reactive crisis response and invest directly in women and youth as active partners in peace efforts.

“Peace is not built in conference rooms alone,” Tkatchenko said. “It is built in communities. It is built through trust. It is built through inclusion. And, ultimately, it is built by people who believe that their differences can be resolved without violence.”

item.title: Marape commends Undialu for successful gun amnesty in Hela
item.description: Prime Minister James Marape has commended Hela Governor Philip Undialu for his leadership in successfully retrieving illegal firearms across the province.
